A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KeyDiff3D work, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 includes Appendices A-E and additional qualitative figures, all inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original Human3.6M measurements and ablations in Tables 1-2, alongside qualitative keypoint, generalization, and object-manipulation results.

after.justification: v2 reports original Human3.6M and CUB experiments, baseline reproductions, robustness tests, computational measurements, and qualitative results throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core diffusion-feature, volumetric keypoint, and animation pipelines remain. Appendix D.1 adds a rotation-based view-invariant consistency loss, weighted 0.1, for Stanford Dogs and CUB. This extends the stated training objective beyond v1's VGG reconstruction and mask losses without replacing the central method.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on CUB-200-2011 birds, including aligned and unaligned images and projected 2D keypoint assessment. Human3.6M, Stanford Dogs, DAVIS, GSO, and AP-10K remain. The bird experiments substantially broaden the represented morphology and quantitative evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds nine 2D comparison methods to the CUB evaluation, including SCOPS, GANSeg, AutoLink, and StableKeypoints (Table 2). It also adds CLIP and DINOv2 feature comparisons and BKinD-3D qualitative comparisons. The Human3.6M comparator membership in Table 1 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces image-size-normalized 2D evaluation on CUB-align and CUB-all, matched-preprocessing baseline retraining, controlled sensitivity protocols, and A6000 timing comparisons. Appendix D.3 reports SAM prompted by provided Human3.6M keypoints and Grounded-SAM2 for animals, revising v1's general Grounded SAM description, although v2's main text retains that older description. These disclosures do not establish rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's feature-extractor and view-count ablations, v2 examines triangulation versus volumetric prediction, additional backbones, keypoint counts, diffusion timesteps, training-set sizes, affine augmentation, camera perturbations, and visibility-based aggregation. Appendices B-C also add concrete failure cases and computational-cost analysis (Tables 3, 5-6; Figures 8-9).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The Gaussian camera-noise levels in v2 are robustness-test settings, not estimates of result uncertainty.

E6.justification: Human3.6M Table 1 errors remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results: CUB-align error 5.16, CUB-all errors 7.7 with four keypoints and 5.5 with ten, plus new ablation, timing, and qualitative findings. The three-view P-MPJPE changes from 86.95 in v1 Table 2 to 86.59 in v2 Table 3. The ResNet-linear ablation row is omitted.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly defines the consistency objective as the average squared discrepancy between original and rotated-volume keypoint projections. The existing projection, aggregation, integral-regression, and skinning mathematics is retained. No theorem, proof, or substantial theoretical analysis is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unsupervised monocular 3D keypoint discovery using multi-view diffusion priors, explicit volumetric features, broad generalization, and manipulation of generated objects. The added bird experiments support these existing contributions rather than redefine their scope.

C2.justification: v1's diffusion-quality and computational-cost limitations are expanded into specific failure cases and measured tradeoffs. v2 adds left-right ambiguity, qualifications about CUB preprocessing comparability, and explanations concerning affine-training shortcuts, visibility errors, and accuracy versus keypoint interpretability. v1's limitation about masking discarding scene context is omitted.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies layer structures, channels, activations, resolutions, reconstruction conditioning, loss weighting, dataset-specific masking and cropping, and inverse coordinate mapping beyond v1's brief implementation paragraph. Appendix A identifies the preprocessing source and controlled baseline reproduction setup, while Table 6 specifies measurement hardware. v2 omits v1's promise of a future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references for bird-keypoint comparisons, ResNet, CLIP, DINOv2, V2V-PoseNet, and preprocessing resources, and removes the Xinyu Yu et al. temporal-consistency reference. The central positioning as extending diffusion-based keypoint discovery to 3D without calibrated multi-view training remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related-work discussion are extensively reworded, especially the distinction between generated supervision and intermediate feature extraction. Experiments are reorganized into separate 3D, animal, and generalization sections, and the limitations discussion is redistributed into expanded appendix analyses. Author and acknowledgment text also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, moves Figure 1 to the first page, redraws the pipeline, replaces the Human3.6M qualitative display with baseline comparisons, and reorganizes animal/generalization panels. It restructures the ablation table and adds CUB, failure-case, sensitivity, computational, and appendix-gallery displays.

improvement.justification: v1 provides mainly qualitative evidence beyond Human3.6M and limited diagnostic and reproducibility detail. v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis through controlled CUB baseline reproductions, targeted robustness analyses, concrete failure cases, measured computational costs, and detailed implementation instructions. These gains improve evaluation and auditability despite unchanged main Human3.6M scores. An important unresolved qualification remains: Appendix D.3's use of provided Human3.6M keypoints needs reconciliation with the annotation-free claims and main-text preprocessing description.
